explain.say: Imagine two babies born on the same day, one in Oslo and one in a village in Malawi. Will their lives be equally easy? Inequality means big differences in income or wealth between people. Look at the board: why do these differences happen?

faq.q: Does where you are born matter?
faq.a: A lot. Economists find that the country you are born in is one of the biggest influences on your lifetime income, along with your family's wealth and education.
asks: Is it luck where you are born?

faq.a: Wealth is everything you own minus what you owe: savings, homes, land, businesses and shares. Income is money coming in each month; wealth is what has built up.
asks: What is the difference between income and wealth?

faq.q: What can governments do about inequality?
faq.a: Options include free education and health care, progressive taxes, minimum wages and cash support for poorer families. Others argue that growth, jobs and lower taxes help most. Countries choose different mixes.
The Gini coefficient measures inequality from 0, where everyone has the same income, to 1 or 100, where one person has everything. South Africa scores about 63; Slovakia and Slovenia about 24.
Many people think some differences are fair if they come from effort and skill, and unfair if they come from discrimination or the luck of birth. Views on how much is acceptable differ widely.

facts: The Gini coefficient runs from 0 (everyone equal) to 1, or 100 (one person has everything).
World Bank data put South Africa's Gini near 63, among the highest, and Slovakia's and Slovenia's near 24, among the lowest.
